text:
Adam Wilsby has gone from fourth-round pick (101st in 2020) to a defenceman Nashville trusts with nearly 20 minutes a night, and his ice time is still climbing, up two minutes over his last ten games. The Predators have won five straight with him playing more than ever, and he scored his first goal of the season in Los Angeles on Monday.

He's one of the fastest skaters in the league (98th percentile in top speed by NHL Edge), and he uses it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 53% of his entries last season and getting to the home-plate area in front of the net for 2.0 chances per 60, 94th percentile. The on-ice results this season are strong: 53% of the expected goals at five on five and the team much better with him than without. His scoring hasn't caught up (six points), and Nashville has also been a bit lucky with him out there, so expect a little give in the results. Evolving-Hockey had him close to replacement level last season. This year looks like a step.
